calls.prompt:
Create ONE 2D fighting-game CHARACTER REFERENCE SHEET of Kharon (the Chainbound), an ORIGINAL character for an original
indie fighting game. It must NOT resemble any existing anime, manga, game or film character.

The FIRST attached image is the approved HOUSE STYLE (another character of this game): copy its rendering exactly - the same
premium high-detail anime fighting-game sprite style, line work, cel shading, metal highlights, proportions, scale and the
same kind of sheet layout - but draw Kharon, NOT the character shown there. The SECOND attached image is Kharon's portrait:
match the face, hair, colours and costume from it.

THE CHARACTER:
A towering giant of a hunter, hunched forward under the weight of his curse, with enormous shoulders, a thick neck and a heavy, scarred, muscular bare torso. Gaunt weathered face with a heavy black brow, deep-set glowing AMBER eyes and a short black beard. Long MATTED BLACK hair falling past the shoulder blades. Weathered TAN skin with raised dark scars across the chest and arms. RUSTED IRON-BROWN chains with dull bronze links are slung diagonally across the chest and wrapped round both forearms. A ragged BLOOD-RED cloth sash hangs over one shoulder and streams down the back in torn strips. Black-brown leather loincloth and trousers, dark leather hip straps, black-brown boots. WEAPON: a huge black GREATBOW nearly as tall as his whole body, a recurve of black lacquered horn on a blackened iron riser, rust-bound tips and a thick dark sinew cord. He holds the bow upright in front of him in his LEFT hand at the wrapped grip, and draws the cord with his RIGHT hand back to the cheek. Black arrows with bronze-brown fletching ride in a hip quiver. Energy and trails: EMBER AMBER streaks with dark grey smoke and orange-red sparks.

ART STYLE: Premium, high-detail anime 2D fighting-game sprite art: the look of a carefully hand-pixelled character sprite rendered at high resolution - crisp deliberate dark outlines (not thick black cartoon lines), cel shading with three to four tones per material, bright specular highlights on metal, a cool rim light, an expressive face with a clear eye, anatomically correct hands with readable fingers, convincing anime anatomy, fluid hair and cloth that follow the motion. Exactly the rendering, palette and level of detail of the attached reference sheet. Not vector art, not blurry, not chibi, no photorealism.

SHEET CONTENT (transparent background, image 1536x1024, no text, no labels, no grid lines, every figure separate):
- top row: full-body neutral stance facing right, towering and hunched, the greatbow held upright in the left hand; a three-quarter close-up of the head with amber eyes, matted hair and beard; a close view of the bow's grip, rust-bound tips and cord
- second row: a combat stance with the bow held low; the full draw with the cord at the cheek; a running pose with chains swinging and the sash streaming; a jump with the bow raised
- third row: an arrow release with an ember-amber trail; a plunge with the bow pointed straight down; a fully drawn power shot with a large ember comet; a crouched guard with the bow held across the body
- bottom row: a hit reaction with chains snapping, a knocked-down pose, a victory pose planting the bow butt-first, the Serpent Rain volley of ember arrows arcing skyward
Every figure faces RIGHT (three-quarter side view like the house style), the same scale (standing height about 240 px), feet on
the same ground line within each row.

LAYOUT (critical - a program slices this sheet):
- Image size 1536x1024, FULLY TRANSPARENT background (alpha), no background colour, no floor, no shadows, no scenery.
- An exact invisible grid of 4 columns x 2 rows of equal cells (384x512 px each). NO grid lines, NO borders, NO text,
  NO numbers, NO labels anywhere.
- Exactly one full-body frame per cell, in reading order (left to right, top row first). 8 frames in total.
- Every frame: the character FACES RIGHT in the same three-quarter side view as the reference; the SAME SCALE in every cell
  (standing height about 399 px from heel to crown, even if a pose is crouched or stretched); the feet rest on the same invisible ground line
  31 px above the bottom edge of the cell (airborne frames are drawn at the SAME place in the cell -
  the game moves the character - just with the airborne pose); the torso stays about 138 px from the cell's
  left edge so a weapon has room in front.
- Nothing (weapon, cape, hair, effects) may cross into a neighbouring cell: keep a clear margin of 8 px at every cell edge, shorten
  the weapon's foreshortening or angle it if needed.
- Consecutive frames are ANIMATION FRAMES of one continuous motion: keep the costume, armour plates, weapon design, hair shape and
  colours identical between frames; only the pose changes.

THIS SHEET: Stance and footwork
  1. combat idle loop 1: fighting stance, weapon ready, knees bent, weight centred
  2. combat idle loop 2: the same stance breathing in, shoulders slightly raised, cape and hair drifting
  3. combat idle loop 3: the same stance at the top of the breath
  4. combat idle loop 4: the same stance breathing out, settling back toward frame 1
  5. standing guard: weapon raised across the body to block, braced, chin down
  6. crouch: low crouch on bent knees, weapon held low and ready (a crouching guard posture)
  7. skid: braking hard from a run, front foot planted forward, body leaning back, cape swinging forward
  8. landing: absorbing a landing from a jump, deep knee bend, one hand low for balance, cape still settling
Character-specific notes for this sheet: The greatbow is always held upright in front of him in the LEFT hand, its lower limb near the ground; the right hand stays empty and relaxed. The chains and the red sash drift with the breath. Keep the bow the same height and angle in all four loop frames.
